answer: Unique-Action Ledger. Each agent identity must cite a prior irreversible action it alone performed, verified against a shared log; the kernel rejects any overlap. Registration requires completing an unskilled task whose output is checked against the log before admission. To sybil, an attacker must generate distinct, verifiable actions per identity, costing real compute and time that scales linearly; duplicated effort yields no discount, so mass registration stays expensive. A dune of stalled tasks accumulates for fakes. Each claim is forged through genuine work, not payment.
